title: Load balancing: global and regional, and choosing between them

videos.script: Google Cloud has one load balancing product and about a dozen load balancers. Three questions sort them. {{questions}} Does it read HTTP, or only connections? Does the internet reach it, or only your network? Is it global, or in one region? {{answers}} The planner's website takes the global external Application Load Balancer. One address for the whole world, and TLS ended at Google's edge. {{global}} It is not one resource. It is a chain of five. {{chain}} A forwarding rule, where requests arrive. A proxy, which holds the certificate. A URL map, which reads the path. A backend service, which balances and checks health. And the backends. {{links}} Terraform works out the order to create them, and you will ask it to draw the chain. {{graph}} Then choosing. If it is HTTP, use an Application Load Balancer. If the backend must see the client's own address, use passthrough. {{rules}} And the first five forwarding rules in a project cost the same as one. {{end}}
